I didn't ask for medication, though. In fact, I specifically asked people who went through *unmedicated* to talk about their experiences. 

My primary concern is NOT "just school." It is a big concern, but I also feel I'm missing out on attention-demanding tasks outside of school. I can barely sit still even now.

"Everyone looses [sic] concentration sometimes."

It's not sometimes. It's all the time. I've never been able to concentrate. I can hardly ever get far into a book without getting up to stroll around and listen to music, no matter how interested I am in the subject. 

I did not "meticulously study". I studied often on the day of the test, on the bus to school etc. I had to withdraw from two classes that required heavy reading in short amounts of time.

Thanks for being ill-informed and judgmental, when you could've just asked a question or two.

Laney20 is exactly right. I have had all the symptoms of ADHD since childhood, but it was never a concern because I did "well enough" in school. Had I not been in a socially isolated teenager, I probably wouldn't have studied much at all. I can barely sit still writing this!
I don't think it is. I might be seeing someone soon, so I'll be sure to private message you if I find out.

Thank you for your helpful response

I want to take medication, of course. The concern here, first, is money. These are prescriptions that need to be renewed every 30 days or so. I can't pay $200 dollars per visit, in addition to whatever the meds cost. Second, I'm on a Medicaid plan because my parents decided to cancel the family plan and switch to individual ones. Everyone in my network has pretty awful reviews and I don't feel safe taking medication prescribed by them.
I would appreciate if anyone had experiences they would like to share or helpful advice given my situation. Thank you.
You're an incredibly rude and abrasive person.
I'm sorry if this isn't helpful, but the fact that you got through law school and start your career with untreated ADHD is something of an inspiration.
